sections.label: Why It Matters in Quant Finance

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Sample spaces, random variables, conditioning, limit theorems — the language every other topic is written in.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Estimation, inference, hypothesis testing and the sampling error that makes backtests lie.

subjects.name: Linear Algebra
subjects.description: Vector spaces, decompositions and eigenstructure — covariance matrices, PCA and risk models all live here.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, Taylor expansion and multivariate analysis, including the Greeks.

subjects.name: Optimization
subjects.description: Convexity, Lagrangians, KKT conditions and numerical solvers behind every portfolio allocation.

subjects.name: Numerical Methods
subjects.description: Finite differences, quadrature, root finding, linear solvers and floating-point pitfalls.

subjects.name: Stochastic Processes
subjects.description: Random walks, Markov chains, martingales, Brownian motion and Itô calculus.

subjects.name: Time Series
subjects.description: Stationarity, ARMA, GARCH, cointegration and forecasting financial data that refuses to be i.i.d.

subjects.name: Econometrics
subjects.description: Regression under real-world violations: endogeneity, heteroskedasticity, panel data, causal inference.

subjects.name: Statistical Learning
subjects.description: Bias–variance, regularisation, cross-validation, trees and neural nets applied to low signal-to-noise data.

subjects.name: Quantitative Trading
subjects.description: Strategy archetypes, edge, capacity, turnover and the economics of a trading business.

subjects.name: Alpha Research
subjects.description: Signal construction, feature engineering, orthogonalisation and honest evaluation of predictive power.

subjects.name: Factor Models
subjects.description: CAPM, Fama–French, statistical factors, risk decomposition and factor crowding.

subjects.name: Portfolio Construction
subjects.description: Mean–variance, Black–Litterman, risk parity, constraints, transaction costs and Kelly sizing.

subjects.name: Risk Management
subjects.description: VaR, expected shortfall, stress testing, drawdown control and the limits of historical risk.

subjects.name: Backtesting
subjects.description: Point-in-time data, look-ahead bias, multiple testing, deflated Sharpe and walk-forward validation.

subjects.name: Alternative Data
subjects.description: Satellite, card, web and text data: sourcing, cleaning, entity mapping, decay and legal constraints.

subjects.name: Derivatives
subjects.description: Forwards, futures, swaps, replication, no-arbitrage pricing and risk-neutral valuation.

subjects.name: Options
subjects.description: Black–Scholes, the Greeks, implied volatility surfaces, exotics and volatility trading.

subjects.name: Fixed Income
subjects.description: Yield curves, duration, convexity, bootstrapping, credit spreads and rates models.

subjects.name: Market Microstructure
subjects.description: Order books, spreads, adverse selection, price impact, market making and queue position.

subjects.name: Execution
subjects.description: Implementation shortfall, VWAP/TWAP, optimal scheduling, slippage and transaction cost analysis.

subjects.name: Programming & Algorithms
subjects.description: Data structures, complexity, vectorised numerics, testing and research code that survives contact with production.

subjects.name: Mental Math & Brainteasers
subjects.description: Fast arithmetic, estimation, expected-value puzzles and the classic trading-floor brainteasers.

tracks.name: Quant Researcher
tracks.description: Statistical depth first. Expect probability, inference, time series and honest evaluation of signals — plus a whiteboard derivation or two.

tracks.name: Quant Trader
tracks.description: Speed, expected value and market intuition. Mental math, probability puzzles, microstructure and risk under pressure.

tracks.name: Quant Developer
tracks.description: Engineering rigour applied to numerical finance: data structures, complexity, numerics, backtest infrastructure and correctness.

tracks.name: Statistical Arbitrage
tracks.description: Cross-sectional and relative-value equity strategies: cointegration, mean reversion, factor neutrality, costs and capacity.

tracks.name: Market Making
tracks.description: Quoting, inventory risk, adverse selection, queue dynamics and the Avellaneda–Stoikov school of thought.

tracks.name: Systematic Macro
tracks.description: Cross-asset trend, carry and value; rates and FX mechanics; regime awareness and drawdown management at low breadth.

tracks.name: Equity Long/Short Quant
tracks.description: Fundamental-meets-systematic: factor exposure, alpha capture, hedging, alternative data and portfolio construction under constraints.

tracks.name: Derivatives & Volatility
tracks.description: Pricing, hedging and the volatility surface: Itô calculus, Black–Scholes and its failures, Greeks, and vol as an asset class.

concepts.title: Bayes' Theorem
concepts.subject: probability
concepts.summary: The rule for inverting a conditional probability — turning "how likely is this evidence if the hypothesis is true" into "how likely is the hypothesis given the evidence".

concepts.title: Brownian Motion
concepts.subject: stochastic-processes
concepts.summary: The continuous-time limit of a random walk — Gaussian, independent increments scaling with √t, nowhere differentiable, and the driving noise underneath essentially every continuous-time model in finance.

sections.label: Why It Matters in Quant Finance

formulas.name: Itô's lemma (one dimension)
formulas.latex:
\d f(t, W_t) = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} + \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x^2}\right)\d t
+ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\,\d W_t

formulas.name: Geometric Brownian motion
formulas.latex:
\d S_t = \mu S_t\,\d t + \sigma S_t\,\d W_t
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
S_t = S_0 \exp\!\left[\left(\mu - \tfrac{\sigma^2}{2}\right)t + \sigma W_t\right]

concepts.title: Covariance & Correlation
concepts.subject: statistics
concepts.summary: Covariance measures how two variables move together in raw units; correlation normalises it to [-1, 1] — together they determine whether combining two positions reduces risk or concentrates it.

concepts.title: Effective Number of Bets
concepts.subject: risk-management
concepts.summary: Diversification is not the number of assets you hold but the number of independent risks you actually bear — measured by the effective dimension of the covariance spectrum and by the entropy of a portfolio's risk contributions across uncorrelated directions.
